problems.problem: On mobile /updates the green kicker becomes indistinguishable from a data ink. `.kicker` is mono / 700 / 11px / 0.11em / uppercase; `.chip` (line 128) is mono / 700 / 11px / 0.1em / uppercase with `color: var(--text-muted)` overridden inline to the category ink when active (MobileUpdates.tsx:97-101), and Tours' ink is `var(--green)` per app/lib/updateInk.ts:18. Worse, `.chipDot` (MobileUpdates.tsx:94) is rendered unconditionally for every category, so the green Tours dot is visible in the rail at all times, not only when Tours is selected. Note 3 defends this by saying the kicker "sits above the h1 in a different band from any tag or chip", and note on the collision only weighs `.liveDot` in `.lastEntry` — but the filter rail is the band immediately after `.hero`, and it is the nearest green on the screen.
problems.correction: Leave mobileUpdates.module.css:80 as it is (or set it to var(--text-muted) if the goal is only to take gold off it). If mobile parity with the desktop rule is wanted, mirror the desktop carrier instead of the desktop hue: add a 22x2px green rule span to the mobile hero and keep the label muted — which is exactly why the desktop change was put on `.eyebrowRule` rather than `.eyebrow`. That does require a .tsx edit, which contradicts note 7's "nothing in this plan changes a .tsx file", so it is a scope decision, not a value swap.

problems.problem: The premise for the desktop stage tint does not hold on the page. The why says the stage and the footnote "sit on the same surface", citing `.sourceBand` at line 543 — that is true (both are `--bg-soft`, byte-identical), but `.sourceBand` is the last band on the page and is never on screen with the summary strip. The surface actually adjacent to `.summaryBand` is `.hero`, and `.hero` at line 398 is `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line)` with NO background — i.e. `--bg`. The summary band is therefore already the only lifted surface at the top of the page and is already distinguished from its neighbour; the 4% wash is solving a collision the reader cannot see. Change 5 does not have this problem: mobileLiveCharts `.hero` (line 68) is padding-only, so there the cells genuinely share `--bg` with the hero directly above them.
problems.correction: Drop change 4, or re-justify it on its own terms (giving the LIVE family its second signature use) rather than on a separation that already exists. If it is kept, it should be kept for the same reason change 5 is kept, and the why should not cite .sourceBand. Change 5 is unaffected and should ship regardless.

problems.problem: The consumer enumeration in the why is incomplete. It names app/afrobeats/[artist]/live/page.tsx as the only other importer of liveCharts.module.css; app/components/LiveReleaseBlock.tsx:4 imports it as well. This does not change the verdict — LiveReleaseBlock is rendered only from live-charts/page.tsx (208, 223) and afrobeats/[artist]/live/page.tsx (274, 289), both LIVE family, and it uses none of the four classes this patch touches — but the plan asserts a complete consumer list that is not complete, and the same assertion pattern is what would let a future swap leak into another family.
problems.correction: No code change needed. Amend the why to list all three importers of liveCharts.module.css (live-charts/page.tsx, afrobeats/[artist]/live/page.tsx, components/LiveReleaseBlock.tsx) and note that LiveReleaseBlock renders only inside those two pages, so the scope claim still holds.

problems.problem: The cited color-mix precedent is not the same construction. The why says "color-mix over a light-dark() token is the established pattern in this repo (globals.css:304, and color-mix on --green already exists at mobileLiveCharts.module.css:289)". Both citations are real but both mix a light-dark() token into `transparent` — globals.css:304 is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--gold-wash-base) 7%, transparent)` and mobileLiveCharts:289 is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 8%, transparent)`. Every other color-mix in the repo does the same. Changes 4 and 5 mix TWO light-dark() tokens together (`var(--green)` into `var(--bg-soft)` / `var(--bg)`), which has no precedent in this codebase. It is spec-valid and resolves correctly wherever light-dark() is supported, so this is a documentation defect rather than a rendering risk.
problems.correction: Either state accurately that this is the repo's first two-light-dark() mix and confirm it renders in both themes before merging, or use the repo's existing shape — `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 4%, transparent)` layered on a surface that is already --bg-soft — so the construction matches the cited precedent exactly.

problems.problem: The card-step change puts .albumCard at the SAME value as its own parent. Discography.tsx:46/50 renders `.pairGrid > .albumCard`, and music/page.tsx:183 puts that pair grid inside `<section className={styles.altSection}>`, which is `background: var(--bg-soft)` (music.module.css:178). Moving .albumCard's rest from var(--bg) to var(--bg-soft) makes the EP cards identical to the band they sit on — the card stops reading as a raised surface entirely, leaving only the 2px --line seams between the two cells and no outer edge at all. This is precisely the collapse the plan's own NOTES cite when excluding .wideCard (music.module.css:280), which is the sibling column in that very same .altSection. The plan applied the corollary to one of the two components in the band and the exclusion to the other.
problems.correction: Scope the rest change to the four-across wall only. Leave line 225 as `background: var(--bg)` and add `.albumGrid .albumCard { background: var(--bg-soft); }`, or keep the line-225 edit and pin the pair grid back by extending the existing rule at line 235 to `.pairGrid .albumCard { padding: 16px; background: var(--bg); }`. Either way the hover at 236 can still go to var(--bg-raised) in both contexts.

problems.problem: The brief's premise is false as the token is declared. `--bg-raised: light-dark(#e6e0d4, #24242a)` against --bg #f7f4ee (line 21), --bg-soft #ffffff (22) and --bg-soft-2 #efeae1 (23) means the light-mode order by luminance is bg-soft(#ffffff) > bg(#f7f4ee) > bg-soft-2(#efeae1) > bg-raised(#e6e0d4). So on paper the new hover/pressed step is DARKER than the inset-track/well token it is supposed to sit above — a raised surface reading deeper than a recess, which inverts the depth ordering §3.1 asserts. Concretely: music.module.css .albumCard's hover flips direction (today #f7f4ee -> #ffffff lightens; after, #ffffff -> #e6e0d4 darkens), and page.module.css:551's homepage catalogue hover goes from a subtle warm lift to a ~7%-darker slab. The plan's own NOTES spot the value but file it as an observation and ship all 21 changes anyway.
problems.correction: Settle the token before applying the sweep. Either re-value light --bg-raised so it sits above --bg and above --bg-soft-2 in the ramp (a warm tint between #f7f4ee and #ffffff, e.g. ~#fbf8f3), or accept a darkening light-mode hover and rewrite the §3.1 text — dropping the 'raised is LIGHTER in light mode too' claim and re-stating the ramp as ordered by depth-of-interaction rather than by luminance. Do not apply 19 hover changes on a premise the token contradicts.

problems.problem: The rationale is wrong and it hides live dead code. The plan says 'the gold .certRow:hover at line 57 is a different, accent-bearing rule and is left alone' — but both `.certRow:hover` blocks (56-60 and 665) are top-level in the SAME CSS module file, so they compile to the same hashed class and both match every .certRow. At equal specificity (0,2,0) the later rule wins, so line 57's gold background is ALREADY overridden and paints nothing today. The same is true of app/records/firsts/firsts.module.css: `.row:hover` at line 12 (gold) is already beaten by `.row:hover` at line 126 (ink), so the 'accent family stays' claim there is also false. Note the non-background declarations at certifications 58-59 DO still apply, so after this change a hovered .certRow gets an opaque --bg-raised fill plus a gold bottom border and a 16px indent — a mixed state nobody designed.
problems.correction: Drop the false rationale from both entries, and fix the collision while you are in the file: either delete the now-provably-dead `background:` declarations at certifications.module.css:57 and firsts.module.css:12, or scope the two definitions apart (`.certGrid .certRow:hover` vs `.groupList .certRow:hover`; `.list .row:hover` for each list) so the gold hover the plan claims to preserve actually renders.

problems.problem: The NOTES defer this line on a misread of the comment. They say globals.css:702 'carries a written 3:1-contrast rationale and is left as-is', but the rationale at lines 696-699 attaches to `border-color: rgba(245, 244, 240, 0.42)` on line 700 — it argues a 0.42-alpha BORDER clears the 3:1 WCAG floor for a control boundary. Nothing in it justifies the 6% white fill on 702. So the stated reason for excluding the rest state does not exist, and shipping 708 alone leaves .btnSecondary with a rest fill that still does not theme (white 6% is invisible on paper) jumping straight to an opaque #e6e0d4 on hover.
problems.correction: Either restate the exclusion honestly ('rest surfaces are out of scope for this pass; 702 goes with the FollowPanel/SearchPalette rest-surface job'), or fold 702 into the sweep as a themed rest fill so the button's two states are designed together rather than one being fixed and the other left broken.

problems.problem: Cited-context line numbers drift by one to two lines in four entries, which will send a reviewer checking the plan to the wrong declaration. .boardBtn's rest `background: var(--bg-soft)` is at line 548, not 549. Likewise: mobileMusic.module.css .albumCover starts at 247, not 249; globals.css's `.segOpt:not(:has(input:checked)):hover` selector is at 1864 with the background declaration at 1865 (the plan labels 1865 as the selector); and certifications.module.css's gold .certRow:hover selector is at 56 with its background at 57. The 21 EDIT targets are all correct — this is only the supporting context.
problems.correction: Correct the four context citations (mobileCerts 549->548, mobileMusic 249->247, globals segOpt selector 1865->1864, certifications gold hover 57->56). No change to any edit target.

problems.problem: The ramp is out of order in light mode. --bg-raised: light-dark(#e6e0d4, #24242a) — on paper #e6e0d4 is darker than --bg (#f7f4ee), darker than --bg-soft (#ffffff) and darker than --bg-soft-2 (#efeae1), so the token the brief describes as 'raised is LIGHTER in light mode too' actually sits BELOW the inset-well step. Every one of the 21 changes inherits this: a hovered card in light is painted a colour reserved-by-position for wells, and music.module.css .albumCard's hover direction flips outright (today #f7f4ee -> #ffffff lightens; after, #ffffff -> #e6e0d4 darkens). The plan files this as a note to confirm and then proceeds anyway.
problems.correction: Block the sweep on the token. Either redefine the light value so it sits above --bg-soft-2 and above --bg-soft in the ramp order the brief states, or get an explicit decision that light-mode hovers darken — and then say so in the token comment, because the current comment ('The hover / pressed surface') does not carry it. Nothing else in this plan should land first.

problems.problem: The .albumCard rest step is moved unscoped, but the class renders in two different beds. Discography.tsx:46 picks .albumGrid or .pairGrid from the same component, and music/page.tsx:183-189 puts the pair layout inside <section className={styles.altSection}>, which is background: var(--bg-soft) (music.module.css:178). After the change the EP cells are painted exactly their own band colour, leaving only the 2px --line seams (rgba alpha .12, 1.31:1, marked DECORATIVE in globals.css:25) to draw the grid — the pair grid dissolves into the band. The plan's own EXCLUDED note refuses this move for .wideCard at line 282 on precisely this reasoning ('moving it to --bg-soft would flatten the card into its own band'), and .wideCard is rendered by the same Discography call block, in the same <section>, twelve lines below the pair grid.
problems.correction: Scope both halves to the ground bed: `.albumGrid .albumCard { background: var(--bg-soft); }` and `.albumGrid .albumCard:hover { background: var(--bg-raised); }`, leaving `.pairGrid .albumCard` on var(--bg) exactly as .wideCard is left — same band, same alternation trick, same answer. Change 15 (line 236) must be scoped with it or the hover starts lifting a card that never stepped up.

problems.problem: .btnSecondary is not a module's hand-mixed hover surface — it is the site's general secondary CTA, used on 25+ call sites across light pages (page.tsx:105 hero, 222/275/315 section heads, music, records, error.tsx:41, not-found.tsx:43). Its hover language is deliberate and accent-only: border-color: var(--gold), color: var(--gold), translateY(-3px), with the fill held identical to rest. Pointing only the hover at --bg-raised gives it an opaque grey-brown fill (#e6e0d4) that in light is DARKER than the ground it sits on and darker still against the white --bg-soft alt bands where several of these buttons live, reading as pressed/disabled inside a gold-outlined pill — while its rest (line 702) stays hardcoded rgba(255,255,255,0.06), unthemed. The result is a half-tokenised pair whose direction inverts between themes, on the one control in this sweep that is a CTA.
problems.correction: Drop this change from the ramp sweep. If the byte-identical rest/hover pair is a real defect, fix it as a button-primitive change that tokenises rest and hover together (and honours the 3:1 boundary rationale written at lines 691-700) — with a designer decision on whether a secondary CTA gets a surface at all, given its hover is currently expressed entirely in gold.

problems.problem: The why says 'the gold .certRow:hover at line 57 is a different, accent-bearing rule and is left alone.' It is not a different rule. This is one CSS module, so .certRow at line 47 and .certRow at line 656 hash to the same class, both blocks are top-level (neither is inside @media), and the later one wins on layout and on hover. The gold hover at 56-60 and its paired .certRow:hover .certTitle gold-title rule at 61 have been dead since the second block landed. Tokenising the winner freezes the ledger's designed gold row hover out of existence, and the diff will read to any reviewer as 'gold preserved'.
problems.correction: Surface the duplicate-block collision before touching it — the two .certRow declarations look like a merge artefact, and which one was meant to survive is a design question, not a sweep question. Either delete the dead block (and lose the gold row hover deliberately, with Paul's sign-off) or restore it and leave line 665 alone. At minimum, correct the why so it does not assert a preservation that is not happening.

problems.problem: Same collision, same false rationale: 'The gold .row:hover at line 12 in the same file is the accent family and stays.' .row is declared twice at top level in one module (lines 4-11 and 120-125), so the gold hover at line 12 — including its padding-left: 14px slide — is already overridden by the ink-wash rule at 126. The plan hardens the winner into --bg-raised and states the gold survives.
problems.correction: Resolve the duplicated .row block first (same call as certifications). Do not tokenise the winner of an unnoticed collision inside a ramp sweep — it converts an accent-family list row into a permanent neutral without anyone deciding to.

problems.problem: The homepage catalogue gets its desktop half only. page.module.css:545 is moved to --bg-soft on the §3.2 argument that cover art must not sit on bare ground, but the mobile homepage renders the same albumCards as the album rail (MobileHome.tsx:274-284): .railItem has no background at all and .railCover paints the Spotify art straight onto the page ground. Both layouts ship in the same document. The plan handled both halves for the music page (music.module.css:225 plus mobileMusic.module.css:242) and then missed the homepage's.
problems.correction: Either give the rail item the same step the desktop card gets (a --bg-soft cell behind .railCover, matching mobileMusic's treatment), or drop the §3.2 photograph-on-ground justification from the page.module.css:545 why and rest it on the card-step rule alone — so the two layouts are decided by the same argument.

problems.problem: The plan invents a remedy for exactly this problem at page.module.css:551 — layering the accent over --bg-raised so an opaque rest does not swallow the gold — then declines to use it here, where the accent carries data meaning. .entryTop is the current No. 1 (background: var(--gold-wash), line 227-229); .entryTop:hover out-specifies it, so hovering the one row people came to find strips its status colour. The plan is right that this already happens today, but it is applying two different answers to one problem inside one change set.
problems.correction: Split the selector: keep .entry:hover on var(--bg-raised), and give .entryTop:hover the same layered form used at page.module.css:551 — `linear-gradient(var(--gold-wash), var(--gold-wash)), var(--bg-raised)` — so the No. 1 row climbs the ramp without losing the colour that says it is No. 1.

problems.problem: Completeness gap in the audit, not an error in it: .release[open] { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--white-wash-base) 1.5%, transparent) } is a hand-mixed neutral state surface in the same file and same idiom as line 223, and it appears neither in the 21 changes nor in the EXCLUDED notes — so a later reader cannot tell whether it was judged and skipped or never seen. It was the only such rule my own parse found beyond the plan's list.
problems.correction: Add one line to the EXCLUDED notes stating that [open] is an expanded state rather than a hover/pressed one and belongs to a later pass (or fold it in if expanded counts as pressed). Either answer is fine; the silence is the problem, given the notes otherwise justify every skip.
